'''James R. Chelikowsky''' is a professor of physics, [[chemical engineering]], and chemistry at [[The University of Texas at Austin]]. He is the director of the Center for Computational Materials at the [https://oden.utexas.edu Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Sciences] at UT Austin. He holds the W.A. "Tex" Moncrief Jr. Chair of Computational Materials.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.utsystem.edu/board-of-regents/former-regents/w-tex-moncrief-jr |title=Profile – W. A. "Tex" Moncrief |publisher=Utsystem.edu |date= 4 January 2022|accessdate=24 April 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==

Chelikowsky is known for his research on the optical and dielectric properties of [[semiconductors]], surface and interfacial phenomena in solids, point and extended defects in electronic materials, pressure-induced amorphization in silicates and disordered systems, clusters and confined systems, and the diffusion and microstructure of liquids.<ref name="test">{{cite web|url=https://www.ices.utexas.edu/people/332/ |title=James Chelikowsky &#124; ICES &#124; U.T. Austin |publisher=Ices.utexas.edu |date= |accessdate=16 August 2013}}</ref>

His current research interests include quantum models for functionalized nanostructures, simulated images from probe microscopies, materials informatics applied to the prediction of novel magnetic materials  and high performance algorithms for solving the electronic structure problem.<ref name="current research">{{cite web|url=http://users.ices.utexas.edu/~jrc/page3/page3.html |title=Research |publisher= |date= |accessdate=19 August 2013}}</ref>

He has published over 450 papers, including five [[monograph]]s,<ref name="publications">{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=jF4rqtEAAAAJ |title=James R. Chelikowsky – Google Scholar Citations |date= |accessdate=16 August 2013}}</ref> and has an h-index of 91.

He earned his BS degree, [[Summa cum laude|Summa Cum Laude]], in physics from [[Kansas State University]] in 1970, a PhD  in physics from the [[University of California at Berkeley]] in 1975. He performed postdoctoral work at [[Bell Laboratories]] from 1976–1978 and was an assistant professor at the [[University of Oregon]] from 1978–1980.  From 1980–1987 he worked at [[Exxon Research and Engineering Company|Exxon Research and Engineering]] Corporate Research Science Laboratories, where he served as group head in theoretical physics and chemistry. In 1987 Chelikowsky  became a professor at the University of Minnesota within the department of chemical engineering and materials science.  He was named an Institute of Technology Distinguished Professor at Minnesota in 2001.  He assumed his current position as the W.A. "Tex" Moncrief Jr. Chair of Computational Materials and professor in the Departments of Physics, Chemical Engineering, and Chemistry and Biochemistry in January 2005.<ref name="education and jobs">{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Chelikowsky&first_nm=James&year=2006 |title=2006 David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics Recipient |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |date=2013-04-16 |accessdate=29 August 2013}}</ref>

He is also a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[Materials Research Society]]. He was also named an outstanding referee for the [[American Physical Society]], a lifetime award.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jim Chelikowsky|url=http://www.ph.utexas.edu/person/chelikowsky_james|publisher=UT Physics|accessdate=29 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130909033002/http://www.ph.utexas.edu/person/chelikowsky_james|archive-date=9 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>
